articleTitle: A millimeter-wave GaAs 5-bit MMIC digital phase shifter
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: This article analyzes the phase shift principle of the monolithic digital phase shifter, and introduces the design method and the structure of each basic shift phase state, and design a 34-36 GHz 5-bit digital phase shifter. Based on the GaAs PHEMT technology, we used ADS Momentum microwave design environment to perform simulations. Finally, the main index of the 5 bit digital phase shifter are: the RMS values of the main shift phase state is less than 2.3 °; Return loss is less than - 14 dB; Insertion loss is within the range of 8.0 ~ 9.1 dB; Insertion loss fluctuations is within the range of - 0.6 ~ 0.4 dB; The chip size is 3.0 mm × 2.0 mm; Control voltage is - 5 v / 0 v. the test result shows that this design method is feasible, and points out that the design needs to be improved in various of models.

articleTitle: A planer sinuous antenna and the relevant balun
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, a planar four-arm sinuous antenna for 2-18GHz and its balun have been studied and designed. The balun, matched the balance structure and the wideband character of the antenna, is microstrip exponential gradual tapered type. The simulation result shows that the VSWR over the frequency band is less than 2. The antenna has good circular polarization performance and for the entire frequency band, the axial ratio can be kept below 3 dB.

articleTitle: Cross-coupled substrate integrated waveguide filter with sharp sideband performance
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, an X-band cross-coupled substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter with sharp sideband performance is proposed. The negative coupling is implemented by 201 TE -mode response in the fourth oversized cavity, which is combined with positive coupling to generate transmission zeros(TZs) for improving the sideband performance.The filter with a passband of 11.5GHz~12.5GHz is fabricated on a single-layer substrate with the standard PCB process. Measured results show that, the in-band insertion loss is 1.2dB, and the stopband attenuation is better than 50dB, it has sharper transition performance at both the upper sideband and lower sideband, compared to the traditional direct coupling SIW filters.

articleTitle: A novel printed UWB and Bluetooth antenna with quad band-notched characteristics
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel printed circle dual-band monopole antenna for Bluetooth and UWB is proposed in this paper. In order to prevent potential interference due to existing nearby communication systems, four rejection bands for 2.6GHz (TD-LTE), 3.3-4.2GHz (WiMAX and C-band communication satellite), 5.2-5.8GHz (WLAN and HIPERLAN/2) and 7.25-7.75GHz (downlink of X-band satellite communication systems) are realized by inserting two SRR-shaped slots into the radiators and adding two parasitic meandered ground stubs closing to the feed-line. The quad notched bands' center frequencies are modulated by changing the size of SRR-shaped slots and parasitic meandered ground stubs. The measured results show this antenna operates at 2.2 to 10.6 GHz, with previous mentioned four bands rejected. Besides, the proposed antenna has a compact size of 33mm*46mm, where these characteristics denote it is fit for mobile devices.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic characteristics simulation of airport runway FOD
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Influenced by various factors, such as radar frequency and incidence angle, the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of airport runway FOD (Foreign Object Debris) targets is very complex. In this paper, a hybrid electromagnetic algorithm is presented and applied in FOD targets electromagnetic scattering simulation. The algorithm can not only reduce the computational complexity but also ensure the simulation accuracy. Simulation results are contrasted in angle domain, frequency domain and material domain, and some analytical conclusions are draw, which is conducive to the engineering design of FOD radar.

articleTitle: DOA estimation in an antenna array with mutual coupling based on ESPRIT
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Many classical direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithms suffer from sensitivity to mutual coupling of antenna array. In this paper, a stable estimation method of DOA estimation is introduced. This method is applying a group of auxiliary arrays, exploiting the banded symmetric and Toeplitz matrix model for the mutual coupling in a uniform linear array (ULA), based on the estimation of signal parameter via rotational invariance techniques (ESPRIT) algorithm. The favorable DOA estimation can be provided without the knowledge of the array mutual coupling matrix. The correction and efficiency of the proposed algorithm are verified by the computer simulation results.

articleTitle: A 0.08–3GHz high gain UWB LNA with improved flatness
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: An ultra-wide band (UWB) low noise amplifier (LNA) of bandwidth 0.08-3GHz, gain more than 28dB, flatness fluctuating in ± 1dB and noise-figure less than 2.3dB is designed and tested. This LNA utilizes the characteristic of reactance value changing with frequency, especially, adopts capacitance negative-feedback in source electrode to compensate the decrease of high frequency gain. Comparing with traditional inductance negative feedback between drain electrode and gate electrode, this adding capacitance feedback can improve gain-flatness obviously. Furthermore, a transmission line of λ/4 is used to achieve broadband match of input and output port, as a result, the voltage standing-wave ratio (VSWR) of input and output port don't exceed 2. Simulated and measured results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: A generalized low power and lower jitter charge pump PLL
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, design a fast locking time and low jitter PLL based on Self-Biased technology. The PLL designs achieve process technology independent, broad frequency range and low input tracking jitter. The loop bandwidth will track operating frequency, therefore, sets no constraint on the operating frequency range. Self-biasing avoids the necessity for external biasing, by generating all of the internal bias voltages and currents from each other so that the bias levels are completely determined by the operating conditions. The PLL is implemented in SMIC 0.13µm MS/RF 1P8M CMOS technology. The design is simulated by a software called Cadance spectre, and the layout is shown. Simulation results show that this circuit can achieve a very wide tuning range is 500MHz to 2 GHz and the phase noise is −91.08dBc/Hz@1MHz, the jitter RMS value is 4.9ps in central frequency at 1.25GHz and the die area of the PLL is 250um × 420um.The power dissipation of the PLL core is only 10mW at a 1.2V supply.

articleTitle: High efficiency dual polarization flat panel antenna for mobile satellite communication
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel dual polarization, high efficiency, waveguide fed flat panel antenna, used as receiving and transmitting antennas for mobile satellite communications, is presented. The detail designs of the element and the feed networks are given. The antenna exhibits high gains and high efficiencies due to the element and the feed networks design. Simulated results for reflection coefficient, gain, isolation and radiation pattern of the antenna are presented. Simulated results show that the designed antenna arrays achieve gains and efficiencies of 31.6 dBi and 80% in Ku band, respectively. The results indicate that the designed antenna is available at millimeter-wave frequencies.

articleTitle: A novel compact dual-band monopole antenna using defected ground structure
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel compact microstrip-fed monopole antenna for wireless application is proposed. Defected ground structure (DGS) is used in this antenna, which has a rectangular patch with dual J-shaped strips, for achieving an additional resonant mode and good impedance matching. The proposed antenna has a small overall size of 20mm×28mm, and operates over the frequency ranges, 2.35-2.75 GHz and 3.3-3.83 GHz suitable for 2.4 GHz WLAN and 2.6/3.5GHz WiMAX communications. Omnidirectional radiation patterns with quite stable gains over the operating bands are obtained, which makes the antenna a good candidate for dual-band wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: A millimeter-wave 6-bit GaAs monolithic digital attenuator with low insertion phase shift
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A millimeter-wave 6-bit GaAs monolithic digital attenuator with low insertion phase shift is presented. This attenuator is fabricated with E.D process, the six main attenuation bits are 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16dB. From the measurement results of this MMIC chip in the 19-23GHz band show that the 6-bit GaAs monolithic digital attenuator has 0.5dB resolution and 35.5dB dynamic attenuation range, return loss are less than -11dB for all attenuation states, and attenuation accuracy: +1.31dB/-0.13dB, insertion phase shift: +3*/-5*; referenced insertion loss <; -2.88dB; the chip size is 3.0mm×2.0mm×0.1mm; the control voltage is 0V-5V.

articleTitle: Compact triple-band monopole antenna with a wide-slot ground for WLAN/WIMAX applications
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A triple-band monopole antenna with a compact size of 28mm×33mm is presented and experimentally discussed for Wireless Local-Area Networks (WLAN) and World Interoperability for Microwave Access (WiMAX) applications. The proposed antenna fed by a 50-Ω microstrip feed line comprises a T-shaped monopole radiating patch and a wide-slot ground plane. With the introduction of a wide slot etched in the ground plane, a second resonant mode is excited at around 2.4 GHz for the T-shaped monopole antenna. And the fact that double symmetrical stubs added to the ground plane provide an upper resonant frequency point at 5.8 GHz leads to the achievement of triple-band operation sufficiently covering the standards of WLAN at 2.4-/5.8-GHz and WiMAX at 2.5-/3.5-GHz. Moreover, a prototype of the proposed antenna is constructed and tested showing good performance across the triple-band range with agreeable simulated and measured results of the return loss, omnidirectional radiation patterns and peak antenna gains.

articleTitle: Compact HMSIW UWB bandpass filter using DGS and EBG technology with two notched-band
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter (BPF) with two notched-band is presented and implemented. Combining half mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) and nonuniform periodic half circle-shaped defected ground structure (DGS), a compact UWB bandpass filter with high selectivity is realized. A modify electromagnetic bandgap structures (EBG) is studied and employed to introduce two notched-bands, which is placed near the feedline to achieve the undesired notched band. The measured BPF insert loss is less than 1.2 dB throughout the pass band from 3.0 GHz to 12 GHz. The measured results demonstrates the validity of proposed UWB filter.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of modulator of a novel rader waveform compatible with communication
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: How to generate a waveform that can realize communication of data and detection of radar at the same time is a key technology of radar-communications integration. In this paper, with the use of existing theory that proposes a novel compatible waveform by modulation LFM signal by MSK, the digital orthogonal modulation MSK-LFM signal is realized on FPGA; and the high-speed DAC and multi-channel synthesis are applied to directly generate wave at UHF-band wave. The algorithms and hardware of the modulator are discussed in detail and the test data is also given.

articleTitle: A method of simulation of ADS-B information source
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: The test of ADS-B receiving equipment is lack of validation of data source, a method of simulation of ADS-B data information is designed aims at the influence of great-cost of outfield test, time consuming and the interference of environment factors. Physical equations are adopted to simulate aircraft's operation, the information of operation of aircraft at a certain moment can be extracted and the information will be coded by the way of RTCA DO-260B coding standard, then the ADS-B message is sent by controlling the time of sending. Result of test shows that this method can simulate a great deal of data and it plays an important role on the performance of quantitative and tests of ADS-B receiver.

articleTitle: 500 ps/1 kV pulse generator based on avalanche transistor Marx circuit
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Ultra-short pulse generator based on Marx circuit, whose switch is avalanche transistor, could generate very short pulse with high peak voltage. The ultra-fast rising-edge of the pulse is mainly determined by transistor's avalanche effect. On the other hand, the avalanche effect have negative influence on the falling-edge, which lead to the waveform unacceptable for signal processing. In this paper, we analyze the oscillation of the falling edge and proposed a method to optimize the waveform of the pulse. Experimental investigation showed that, by optimizing the charging capacitors, pulse width can be effectively reduced and the waveform of the pulse is more close to zero order gaussian pulse.

articleTitle: Substrate integrated waveguide cross-coupling filter with multilayer hexagonal cavity
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Hexagonal cavities and their applications to multilayer substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filters are presented. The hexagonal SIW cavity which can combine flexibility of rectangular one and performance of circular one is convenient for bandpass filter's design. Three types of experimental configuration with the same central frequency of 10 GHz and bandwidth of 6%, including third-order and four-order cross-coupling topologies, are constructed and fabricated based on low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology. Both theoretical and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Design of a high gain Axial-mode helical antenna with a loaded plate
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A high gain Axial-mode helical antenna with a loaded plate is proposed. A metal plate is inserted on the end of the helix as a loaded element to improve the gain of the proposed antenna without adding the number of turns. A prototype of the proposed antenna is manufactured according to the optimal results and measured. Compared with the traditional helical antennas, the results show that the gain of the helical antenna with a loaded plate can be enhanced obviously at the operating band without increasing the antenna axial length.

articleTitle: Compact multiband antenna employing CRLH-TL structure for USB dongle applications
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: By employing composite right/left handed transmission line (CRLH-TL) structure, the proposed antenna for wireless universal serial bus (USB) dongle applications can provide two wide operation bands (746-960 and 2500-2690 MHz) to cover the LTE700/GSM850/900 and the LTE2500 operation. The proposed antenna utilizing a limited space of 12 × 28 × 5.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> consists of a folded monopole and a CRLH-TL structure. Detailed operating principle of the proposed antenna including the effects of the laptop and the equivalent circuit for CRLH-TL structure is discussed.

articleTitle: A broadband curvilinear dipole based on non-foster matching network
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A broadband curvilinear dipole is presented, and impedancematching network including Non-Foster elements is employed to broaden its bandwidth. The antenna is precisely designed in a curved shape with the dimension of 1100 mm × 85 mm. The bandwidth for VSWR less than 2 ranges from 290MHz to 765MHz. Then, a conventional LC matching network is designed for the antenna, which brings a bandwidth of 5 octaves covering from 258MHz to 1370MHz. And then, the Non-Foster elements are introduced into the matching network, which makes it possible to include both positive LC and negative LC in the network. The simulate results show that the bandwidth of the antenna with Non-Foster Matching Network covers 14 octaves ranging from 116MHz to 1600MHz. The gain of the antenna is higher than 3dB, and the antenna exhibits a good omni direction radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: The research on the design of the RF front-end for the LTE - Advanced mobile terminals
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: LTE-Advanced technology is required to support 100MHz channel bandwidth and transfer rates in excess of 1Gbps. The 2.6GHz band is one of the core band of LTE-Advanced technology. This paper provide the detailed design of the RF front-end. The receiver uses the traditional double-conversion superheterodyne structure, while transmitter uses a zero-IF structure, able to obtain high receiver sensitivity and channel selectivity and small size. The tests' results show that the overall system performance is generally satisfactory. In the transmitter, the maximum output power is up to 23dBm and IMD3 is better than 45dB, for the 100MHz 16-QAM signal, the modulation accuracy is better than 4.18%; in the receiver, the gain flatness is less than 2.66dB, for the 5MHz 16-QAM modulated signals within the passband, the modulation accuracy is better than 1.34%. The transceiver switch time is less than 1.72μs.

articleTitle: A DDS-based C-band wideband agile frequency synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, a DDS-based C-band wideband agile frequency synthesizer is described. The DDS (Direct Digital Synthesizer) is used to achieve agile frequency hopping. The output of DDS is combined with four independent PLLs, which generate low phase noise LO signal, to expand the bandwidth. Measured results show that the frequency hopping time is shorter than 500ns. The spur suppression is better than 60dB and the phase noise is lower than -104dBc/Hz@10kHz from 6.84~7.956GHz.

articleTitle: Design of wideband triangular patch antenna with modified ground plane
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel coplanar probe-fed patch antenna with a modified ground plane for wideband applications is proposed. The antenna consists of two symmetrical corrugations beside the triangular patch radiator and a U-shaped ground plane. A significant improvement on the impedance bandwidth up to about 4:1 can be obtained. The experimental impedance bandwidth, determined by -10dB reflection coefficient, is greater than 114% (0.66 to 2.41 GHz). The proposed antenna has a small overall size of 0.62λ × 0.46λ × 0.19λ and a patch size of 0.56λ × 0.28λ at 1.45 GHz (center frequency). Good agreement between the measurement and simulation has been achieved. Meanwhile, the proposed antenna exhibits good broadside radiation characteristics over the whole operating bandwidth. Details of the proposed design and experimental results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Compact SIW bandpass filter for wideband millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: a compact substrate intergrated waveguide (SIW) bandpass filter (BPF) is proposed for millimeter-wave (mmW) application. Four vias are located inside the SIW cavity in the form of rotationally symmetrical structure to provide transmission zeros at upper-stopband. As design examples, one substrate integrated waveguide bandpass filter prototype using Low Temperature Co-fired Ceramic (LTCC) on single layer substrate is designed and experimentally examined. The measured results show that the filter achieves a passband insertion loss of 0.8 dB at 50 GHz, return loss below -13dB and 3-dB fractional bandwidth of 30%.

articleTitle: A 2.4-GHz RFIC-on-chip antenna on flexible surface proximate to the human body for miracast and wireless application
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A 2.4-GHz RFIC-on-chip antenna in 0.18 um CMOS 1p6M process is presented. The HFSS 3-D EM simulator is employed for design simulation. A printed 2.4GHz antenna has been realized by using the CMOS RFIC-on-chip. The measured VSWR is less than 2 from 2.4- to 2.483-GHz. The measured phase distribution of the input impedance is quite linear and the H-plane patterns are almost omnidirectional. The Kirchhoff's surface integral representation (KSIR) was adopted in the developed FDTD code to compute the far field distributions from the near filed ones in time-domain. For the biometry applications the investigation of the body effect on the antenna radiation characteristics is achieved. The human tissue includes single layer of muscle and three-layer tissue. Simulated results illustrate that the included current in fat layer is very small due to the lower dielectric constant and conductivity. After adding a floating metal, the absorbed energy of human tissue will be reduced. The chip area is 0.495 (0.75×0.66 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>).

articleTitle: A low-profile two-arm Archimedean spiral antenna radiating a circularly polarized normal beam or conical beam
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A two-arm Archimedean spiral antenna (TAS) is proposed to provide a circularly polarized (CP) normal beam or conical beam. The antenna is fed by coaxial lines without a balun circuit. When it is excited out of phase, a CPnormal beam which is almost symmetric with respect to the antenna axis is produced. While excited in phase, it radiates a CP conical beam. The antenna height is chosen to be extremely small to realize a low-profile antenna. The simulated results show that the antenna has a good VSWR and a good axial ratio over the frequency range of 1.8GHz to 2.1GHz.

articleTitle: Study of the characteristic of gap waveguide and comparison with rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental verification of the ridge gap waveguide, appearing in the gap between parallel metal plates. It also describes the basic ideas of how local waveguides and transmission lines can propagate along desired paths in the air gap between two metal surfaces. The principle of operation is related to the performance of artificial magnetic conductors, AMC surfaces and soft and hard surfaces. And by evaluating the quality factor, a study and quantification of losses in ridge gap waveguide compared to losses in ideal standard rectangular waveguide is also presented.

articleTitle: A fast algorithm for long code direct acquisition
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In GPS (Global Position System), direct acquisition of the GPS P(Y)-code is a two-dimension lengthy searching process in time and frequency dimension. CCPAZP-FFT (Circular Correlation by Partition And Zero Padding) uses FFT to achieve parallel correlation and frequency searching. In this way acquisition can be achieved very fast as it transfers two-dimensional search into parallel one-dimensional search. However, correlation points are still too much and Computation is heavy. This paper proposes an improvement algorithm of combination of CCPAZP-FFT and XFAST. This way Compares to CCPAZP-FFT is reduced by two thirds of the computation in order to achieve rapid long code acquisition.

articleTitle: Research on 60 GHz optical millimeter-wave over fiber system using two cascaded Mach-Zehnder modulators
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A frequency sexualizing technique for the generation of millimeter-wave (mm-wave) is proposed and investigated. The proposed technique is comprised of two cascaded dual-electrode Mach-Zehnder modulators (MZMs). The first MZM, biased at minimum transmission, is only used for optical carrier suppression modulation, and the second MZM, biased at maximum transmission, is used for both even-order optical harmonic generation and data signal modulation. From the theoretical analysis and simulated demonstrations, it is concluded that using an RF signal at 10 GHz, which carries the data signal and drives the MZMs, an mm-wave signal at 60 GHz can be obtained. The power penalty is less than 1 dBm after 50 km SMF transmission, mostly because of the higher optical harmonic distortion suppression ratio (OHDSR).

articleTitle: Compact bandpass filter with wide stopband utilizing modified anti-parallel coupled-lines
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel bandpass filter with a wide stopband is presented. The proposed filter mainly consists of modified anti-parallel coupled-lines and four open circuited stubs, which can generate multiple transmission zeros at the lower and upper stopbands. Therefore, a wide stopband characteristic can be achieved. The central frequency of this proposed filter, which is implemented on Roges 4350 substrate, is at 2.5 GHz with an insertion loss of less than 1.8 dB and a 3 dB bandwidth of 4%. Good suppressing of more than 28 dB is obtained in lower stopband from DC to 2.3 GHz, and the upper stopband has larger than 18 dB rejection in the range of 2.7 GHz to 10 GHz. Measured results show a good agreement with simulated results.

articleTitle: Rectangular waveguide band-pass filter with harmonic suppression
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: An improved structure of rectangular waveguide band-pass filter with harmonic suppression is proposed. The filter consists of cascade resonant cavities with coupling provided by irises. By means of varying the width of each resonator and the offsets between the adjacent resonant cavities, the stop-band was successfully pushed to a two octaves frequency range. The results show that the designed rectangular waveguide band-pass filter has a pass-band of 27.5 GHz – 30 GHz and stop-band suppression of greater than 33 dB over the frequency range from 35 GHz to 60 GHz, its pass-band insertion loss is less than 0.1 dB, return loss is more than 19 dB. The filter can be used in modern communication systems with the requirement of harmonic suppression.

articleTitle: FPGA implementation of RVFTDNN for digital predistortion
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Hardware implementation of real-valued focused time-delay neural network (RVFTDNN) in FPGA for digital predistortion is presented in this paper. The predistorter implemented in field programmable gate array (FPGA) using RVFTDNN is obtained based on model inverse with indirect learning scheme and trained offline with Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm. Measurement results show that more than 10dB improvement of adjacent channel power ration (ACPR) performance of the power amplifier (PA) can be obtained for single carrier WCDMA signal.

articleTitle: Analysis of beam pointing error of retrodirective array in the presence of multiple sources
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Beam pointing error variety with the angle of incoming signals of the retrodirective array in the presence of multiple sources is discussed in this paper. The influences of the number of the array and the distances between adjacent elements are analyzed. The simulation results can be used as the theoretical evidence of the array for assisting design where a specifically beam pointing error are required.

articleTitle: A new band-notched UWB antenna based on EBG structure
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this letter, a new band-notched ultra wideband (UWB) antenna based on electromagnetic band gap (EBG) technology has been designed and analyzed. The EBG structure is applied in a UWB antenna to create a stop band and it is located between the microstrip feedline and the ground plane. EBG characteristics, such as the reflection phase and the transmission coefficient S21, are studied. At the end of this paper, physical model and measured results are presented and measured results are well matching with simulated ones. And several main parameters of proposed antenna are analyzed and discussed in detail.

articleTitle: A high-gain LTCC horn antenna with different feeding structures
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, a 30GHz horn antenna with different feeding structures is discussed based on low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology. The antenna with high gain is first designed by analyzing operation mechanisms of horn antennas and its implementation on LTCC structures. Then, radiation patterns are studied under stripline and microstrip feedings. The achieved fractional bandwidth is from 28.3 to 32.6 GHz (about 16%), and the simulated gain is 6.55 dBi with beam width of 90 degree at 30 GHz. The proposed horn antenna can be easily integrated with front-end circuits or systems, which is a great improvement over traditional horn antennas.

articleTitle: The research of Distributed Phased-Array target localization based on Joint-Esprit algorithm
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Distributed Phased-Array Radar is a new radar system with multiple radars working together. This radar system mainly effects in weak targets precise detection and identification of wide range space. This paper briefly introduces the structure and working process of distributed phased-array radar, according to the targets localization requirement and working characteristic of distributed phased-array radar, Joint-Esprit localization algorithm is proposed. Using the high precision characteristic of Esprit spectrum estimation algorithm, targets localization is very precise. And search function is proposed in single target model and multi-targets model. Through the simulation, the Joint-Esprit target localization algorithm can locate the target accurately.

articleTitle: Molecular dynamics simulation on temperature and structure characteristics of microwave-heating NaCl solution
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, we performed a series of molecular dynamics simulations to study the temperature characteristics of heating NaCl solution at different concentrations by using different electric field intensity of microwave. By fitting the obtained data, we have established an empirical formula of temperature rise, which can simulate the temperature characteristic of heating NaCl solution under a microwave frequency of 20GHz within the span of molecular dynamics simulation. By comparing and analyzing the pair distribution functions obtained under microwave heating and conventional heating, we found that there is no non-thermal effect during microwave heating NaCl solution.

articleTitle: A compact monopole antenna for Bluetooth and UWB applications with dual band notched characteristics
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel compact ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna with Bluetooth pass band and dual notched bands for wireless applications is presented. The low-profile antenna comprises of a pentagonal-shaped patch for covering UWB band (3.1~10.6 GHz). A lower pass band, 2.4 GHz Bluetooth band (2.4~2.484 GHz), can be realized by etching a pair of meander slot at the both sides of ground plane without affecting its UWB behavior. By etching a U-shaped slot on the radiator and symmetrically employing two parasitic strips at each side of the radiator, two-band rejected filtering properties in the WLAN are achieved. The proposed antenna is designed and built on a FR-4 substrate, with overall size of 26 mm×30 mm. Experimental results show that the designed antenna successfully adds a pass band of 2.4 GHz Bluetooth band and two rejection bands of 5.2/5.8 GHz WLAN. Moreover, the antenna has good omnidirectional radiation patterns in the H-plane.

articleTitle: A novel mixed and cross-coupled bandpass filter based on Stepped-Impedance-Resonator
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: An improved stepped impedance resonator (SIR) is proposed in this paper. Due to this improved resonator, mixed coupling is obtained in filter design. Additional transmission zero is achieved base on new added coupling path. The proposed resonator was adopted to instead one resonator in conventional fourth-order cross-coupled filter. Base on proposed filter topology, a four-pole bandpass filter both with mixed-coupling and cross-coupled have been fabricated and measured. Advantages of this filter not only its sharp rejection, but also its spurious suppression with multi-zeros.

articleTitle: Band-notched UWB monopole antenna design using a shorted parallel coupled strip
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A monopole UWB antenna with band-notched function is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a modified rectangular radiator and a truncated ground plane. To generate a notch around 5.5GHz WLAN band, a quarter-wavelength shorted parallel coupled strip is attached to the feed line. With those designs, the antenna yields an impedance bandwidth of 2.8 to 13.1 GHz (VSWR < 2), while showing rejection performance in the frequency band of 5.1 to 5.9 GHz. Experimental results show that the proposed antenna has suitable impedance bandwidth, good radiation patterns, stable gain across the working bands.

articleTitle: Optimal design of loop bandwidth in GPS/INS deeply integration
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: The typical tracking loops of the GPS/INS deeply integration are unable to track the signals under high dynamic environments. The crux of the integrated system performance is the low-order phase-locked loops (PLL). Once the environmental dynamics exceed a threshold, the tracking loops will lose the assistance of GPS. The conflict between the ability to track the signal and improving PLL tracking performance should be compromised in PLL design. Aiming at this issue, the design of loop bandwidth is vitally important in the GPS/INS integrated system design. To achieve the successful performance, this paper presents the deeply integration tracking loop design based on a third-order PLL, also included is the stability analysis of the tracking loop. Experimental result shows that the bandwidth of such type of tracking loops could be lower than 3Hz.

articleTitle: A novel UWB band-pass filter with selectivity improved by modified resonant-type composite right/left-handed structure
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel Composite Right/Left Handed Transmission Line (CRLH-TL) ultra-wideband band-pass filter (UWBPF) is proposed in this paper. The filter is composed of a complementary split ring resonator (CSRR), a pair of quarter-wave slot resonator circuit (QWSRC) and radial stub (RS). Besides the two transmission zeros introduced by the QWSRC and the RS for better upper stop-band rejection, the CSRR creates another transmission zero to improve lower stop-band selectivity. In addition, detailed analysis based on image parameter method is given. The fractional bandwidth (FBW) is designed to be 100%. The measured results show good rejection of more than 22 dB in the lower stop-band and 32 dB in the upper stop-band from 6.9GHz to 9.6GHz, which are in good agreement with simulated results.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of higher-mode face shear square micromechanical resonators
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Polysilicon face shear (FS) square micro-mechanical resonators based on MEMS technology operating in second-mode have been studied at frequency 70MHz. By carefully designing the electrodes and the exact support beam locations that minimize the anchor loss, these resonators actually achieved higher quality factor Q (exceeding 20,000 with straight beam support) in the second-mode than in the fundamental at the same frequency. With larger dimensions than previous fundamental mode counterparts, these second-mode face shear square resonators show many advantages over the former, such as (1) lower series motional resistance R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>; (2) higher Q; (3) very high maximum vibration amplitude (achieved 4.8nm with 1μm gap size), which is directly proportional to the output current i<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and maximum vibration energy that a resonator can be stored. So that, the second-mode face shear square resonator is highly recommended when designing a face shear square resonator at high frequency.

articleTitle: Research on WCDMA RF front-end technology
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A kind of WCDMA RF front-end of mobile table is designed in this paper. The main building blocks of this RF front-end are receiving circuit, transmitting circuit, duplexer and regulator. A cascade mode with three LNAs is used in the receiving circuit, and a traditional cascade mode with driver amplifier and power amplifier is used in the transmitting circuit. The final measurement results show that this RF front-end provides maximum transmitting power of 23dBm, power conversion gain of receiving circuit of 40dB, power conversion gain of transmitting circuit of 25dB, gain flatness of less than 1dB, input and output return loss of more than 10dB, output P1dB of 32dBm, ΔIMD3 of −48dBc, and ACLR of −46.29dBc (lower sideband) and −48.56dBc (upper sideband). Therefore, this RF front-end completely meet the standards of WCDMA, which could be installed in the mobile table to use.

articleTitle: Tree-like metamaterial microstrip antenna for gain enhancement
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel high-gain patch antenna using tree-like fractal metamaterial structure has been designed. Simulated results show that the tree-like metamaterial structure has the property of the negative permeability. The proposed fractal antenna was constructed by changing the substrate of traditional patch antenna with the tree-like structure. The measured impedance bandwidth of the antenna is about 7.2%. The fractal antenna gain was enhanced by 1.8dB comparing with the conventional microstrip antenna, and the 3dB beamwidth of the E-plane was reduced by 16.2°. The tested results are in good agreement with that of the simulation.

articleTitle: A method for loop-circuit stability analysis
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A method for loop circuit stability analysis is introduced through investigating its closed-loop admittance and open-loop impedance. This method has wider adaptability and less limitation than the traditional approach which uses open-loop power-wave transfer function. A 6-GHz HBT oscillator is designed to verify this method. The measurement result shows the effeteness of the proposed method while the traditional method fails.

articleTitle: A high-linearity S-band SiGe HBT low-noise amplifier design
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A 2.1∼2.5GHz SiGe HBT low-noise amplifier (LNA) with highly linearity and low-noise is described. The LNA is designed with a novel resistor feedback bias circuit structure which be aimed to obtain excellent linearity performance. On-chip balun is used for single-to-differential conversion between the LNA and the down-conversion mixer. The simulated results show that the transmission gain is 11.9dB with less than 0.3dB variation in 60M frequency range, noise figure varies between 1.9 and 2.1dB, input reflection (S11) is less than −16.3dB and the Op<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> is more than 16dBm over the entire band. Power dissipation is 60mWat 5V supply.

articleTitle: UWB asymmetric multi-section directional coupler with improved directivity
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: An ultra-wideband (UWB) asymmetric multi-section directional coupler is proposed and demonstrated. In order to obtain broadband frequency response an asymmetric offset parallel-coupled strip transmission line coupler has been chosen. The influence of discontinuities in the regions of coupled and transmission line connections, as well as intersection connections, has been taken into account in the design stage. The proposed procedure allows to achieve a very significant improvement, particularly for the directivity and return loss characteristics by using the recently developed capacitive compensation technique to compensate the parasitic reactance associated with the discontinuities. A 15-dB coupler over the frequency range from 2 to 18 GHz is designed, fabricated and measured. The compensation technique has been applied for the design of directional couplers with the coupling value of 15 dB. Design consideration and simulated as well as measured results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A compact broadband high-power PIN limiter using LC network
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A compact broadband high-power limiter is proposed in this paper. The limiter has a two stages structure which composed of different PIN diodes. A broadband LC impedance transformation network is employed in limiter to replace traditional quarter-wavelength line. This limiter has smaller size and higher isolation compared with traditional one in low frequency. To verify proposed structure, a limiter is fabricated and measured. At small signal level, insertion loss of proposed limiter is less than 0.6 dB measured from 200 MHz~800 MHz. At large signal level, isolation is 29 dB for a 700 MHz 15 W input power, which is 3 dB higher than the traditional limiter.

articleTitle: A Ka-band transceiver based on LTCC technology
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: This paper describes a Ka band transceiver based on low temperature cofired ceramics (LTCC) technology. The proposed transceiver is implemented with 1.3mm substrate with all the passive elements as well as naked millimeter wave MMICS integrated in multilayer LTCC. The whole size of the transceiver is 78.3mm×57.6mm×17.3mm. The fabricated transceiver reveals a transmit power of about 30dBm and the receiving section has greater than 26dB of gain and less than 5dB NF.

articleTitle: Design of compact UWB planar antenna with dual band-notched for WLAN and WiMAX
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A compact planar ultrawideband (UWB) antenna with dual band-notched characteristics is proposed and investigated in this paper. The proposed antenna utilized a T-shaped stub on the radiating patch and U-shaped slot on ground to generate two notched bands at 3.5 GHz and 5.5 GHz, which perform good rejection of interference with worldwide interoperability for microwave access (WiMAX) and wireless local area network (WLAN). The antenna is studied and optimized using computer simulation. The results which show good performance are provided.

articleTitle: Miniaturized dual-band bandpass filter with wide stopband using stepped impedance resonators
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A compact dual-band bandpass filter with wide stopband based on stepped impedance resonators has been presented. The proposed filter consists of two quarter-wavelength modified SIRs which share a common grounded via-hole and two symmetrical open-end stubs. This structure without the open-end stubs can generate four transmission zeros (TZs) to achieve strong passband selectivity and the additional two transmission zeros can be obtained to improve the wide stopbabnd characteristics by using the symmetrical open-end stubs. The center frequencies and bandwidths of the two passband can be controlled by adjusting the geometric dimensions of the proposed SIRs. Moreover, The filter with passbands operated at 2.4/5.2 GHz can finely meet the wireless local area network (WLAN) bands requirements. The circuit only occupies 0.07 λg×0.11 λg.

articleTitle: A compact dual polarized UWB diversity wide-slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A compact dual-polarized printed ultra-wideband (UWB) wide-slot antenna for multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO)/ diversity application is proposed. The wide-slot antenna built on a printed circuit board (PCB) consists of two right-angled trapezoid radiation patches with two orthogonal feeding ports. High isolation is achieved by placing a short strip at the middle of the slot and etching an isosceles triangle on the ground plane. Measured results show that the isolation is better than 20 dB across the entire working band from 3-11 GHz. The envelope correlation coefficient between radiation patterns shows consistent diversity performance across the whole UWB band. These features make this proposed antenna very attractive for the application of diversity systems. Besides, the antenna has a compact size of 50mm*50mm, which is a good candidate for portable devices.

articleTitle: Compact box-section bandpass filter with enhanced stopband characteristics
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A compact bandpass filter (BPF) with enhanced stopband characteristics is presented in this paper. The proposed BPF consists of four improved stepped impedance resonators (SIRs),which implements into a box-section strcture. To improve the frequency selectivity and the stopband characteristics, additional transmission zero (TZ) was introduced by mixed electric and magnetic (EM) coupling. A new filter with 31.2% fractional bandwidth (FBW) has been designed and fabricated to verify the validity of the proposed method. The filter has two transmission zeros, where TZ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> is located in 0.4GHz with 78.7dB rejection and TZ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is located in 2.7GHz with 50.2 dB rejection. Measured results are in good agreement with the electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: MIM serie capacitor model for MMIC design application
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A new proposed Metal-Insulator-Metal (MIM) serie capacitor model for Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit is presented. The MIM serie capacitor model covers the frequency range up to 40 GHz for millimeter-wave circuit design application. The parasitic elements of model are extracted by parameters fitting optimization between the measured S-parameters and model simulated result. The relationship between the optimized parasitic element values and the dimension data of capacitor structure can be expressed.

articleTitle: Performances analysis of a compact slot-coupled UWB directional coupler
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, based on the performances analysis of bent couplers, An improved 3dB three-section slot-coupled bent coupled operating over a bandwidth from 0.6 to 1.8 GHz is presented. The proposed couplers are constructed by two symmetrical three-section microstrip lines, coupled by slot between them. The simulated and measured of S-parameters and phase imbalance results are presented with good agreement.

articleTitle: A novel 1∶19 microstrip radial power divider design for the application in antenna array
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel microstrip radial 1:19 power divider is proposed in this paper. The conventional impedance transformation method is used here with a single substrate to realize 1 to 19 power transmission. To verify our design, the power divider is fabricated and tested. It can be observed that it achieves 29.4% impedance bandwidth (VSWR<;2), the transmitted magnitude and phase imbalance for 19 outputs are ±0.1 dB and ±1 deg, respectively.

articleTitle: Recursive KA-STAP algorithm based on QR decomposition
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: The performance of space-time adaptive processing (STAP) for airborne radar decreases due to the nonstationarity of clutter in heterogeneous clutter environment. To solve this problem, a knowledge-aided space-time adaptive processing (KA-STAP) algorithm based on QR decomposition is proposed in this paper. It is a fast recursive algorithm implemented in the data domain directly without sample matrix inverse (SMI). The simulation results show that the recursive KA-STAP algorithm based on QR decomposition has the same weight vector with the SMI algorithm and better clutter suppression performance compared with traditional STAP.

articleTitle: Stability analysis for a class of fractional singular systems with nonlinear disturbances
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: This paper studies the stability of fractional singular systems with nonlinear disturbances. By using Lyapunov stability theory, we obtain sufficient conditions for the asymptotic stability of the systems.

articleTitle: A novel omega-shaped microstrip slow-wave structure for 60-GHz traveling-wave tube
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, a novel microstrip meander-line slow-wave structure (SWS) is proposed for using in V-band traveling-wave tube (TWT). The new omega-shaped microstrip meander-line slow-wave structure has higher interaction impedance by contrasting analysis of the conven-tional U-shaped microstrip meander-line SWS. The transmission characteristics, dispersion characteristic, coupl-ing impedance and beam-wave interaction are simulated by utilizing the simulation software HFSS and CST. The calculation of beam-wave interaction indicated that, at a beam current of 0.1 A and a beam voltage of 7.1 kV, the new microstrip meander-line SWS is capable of delivering more than 28.5 W output power. And its interaction efficiency reaches 12.3% with a transient 3dB bandwidth of 5 GHz (ranging 57.5 GHz to 62.5 GHz).

articleTitle: A 2.6 GHz Class-E power amplifier design
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A design of switching power amplifier (PA) with high efficiency and considerable output power is reported. This power amplifier is based on commercial available GaN HEMT device. Design process based on Source/Load Pull technique is described in detail. The simulation results show that the proposed amplifier achieves drain efficiency of 85%, power added efficiency of 82.5% and 40 dBm output power at 2.6 GHz. This power amplifier could be applied to TD-LTE base station.

articleTitle: Novel wideband LNA with improved anti-burnout performance
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Based on the burning mechanism of the device, novel clipper circuit is introduced to the design of LNA. The clipping diodes were placed in parallel with the gate of transistor, and absorbed into the input matching circuit of LNA. Finally, the influence of the characteristic impedance of series microstrip in input matching circuit on the anti-burnout performance of LNA is discussed. The results of simulation and experiment proved that the introduction of the clipper circuit can significantly improve the anti-burnout ability of the LNA. Microstrip in input matching circuit on the anti-burnout performance of LNA is discussed. The result of simulation and experiment proved that the introduction of the clipper circuit can significantly improve the anti-burnout ability of the LNA.

articleTitle: Flocking algorithms for multi-agent systems with time-delay
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Focusing on the time-delay problem of multi-agent systems, this paper provides solutions for flocking of systems with time-delay. For the circumstance with a virtual leader, the agents would follow the virtual leader and achieve the same velocity asymptotically. Systems with homogeneous and inhomogeneous time-delays are discussed respectively. The appropriate simulation circumstance is set up, and the obtained results are in agreement with the theoretical deduction, which show the effectiveness of the proposed flocking algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of a 16GHz TE11-HE11 mode converter in smooth-walled circular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: The traditional TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode conversion is usually achieved in a circumferentially corrugated waveguide with varying slot depth, which is easy to bring about microwave breakdown due to the machining burrs at the high frequency. In order to avoid this defect, the smooth-walled structure with a gradual change of the radius is given in this paper. Based on the mode coupling theory, a 16 GHz TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode converter constituted by parabola-profile and sin-profile has been designed by numerical calculation, it also has been testified by electromagnetic simulation software. The simulation results are consistent with the numerical calculation results. The bandwidth of the designed mode converter is over 1.8 GHz, and the relative bandwidth is about 11%, the conversion efficiency at 16 GHz could reach 99.21%.

articleTitle: Design of millimeter-wave receiver array
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Using millimeter wave receiving antenna array, attenuator, detector and accessory device design of millimeter wave receiving array, in order to realize the millimeter wave high power beam spot testing function. First, completed the overall design of the millimeter wave receiving array, the second focuses on the design of millimeter wave receiving antenna array. Antenna array through CST software simulation, respectively, analyzed different open forms the antenna unit, different waveguide length L of the gain, receive power and caused by the installation position offset. Through the simulation, found some useful rules for millimeter wave receiving antenna array design. To determine the size and position precision of the antenna unit, completed the millimeter wave receiving array processing.

articleTitle: Design of a high efficiency W-band extended interaction oscillator
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: This paper designed a high efficiency W-band extended interaction oscillator. The rectangle coupled-cavity slow-wave line along with the sheet beam can increase the impedance of the circuit and has the merit of high power operation. Through PIC simulation the optimized parameters has been achieved with the beam-wave interaction efficiency over 27%.

articleTitle: A 2.1–2.5 GHz high linearity and low noise down-conversion active mixer
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: This paper presents a high-linearity and low-noise down-conversion active mixer at 2.1-2.5 GHz for a receiver with low conversion gain. This proposed circuit has been designed and fabricated with a 0.35 μm SiGe BiCMOS process. The layout size is 0.34 × 0.3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Through simulation, the designed mixer achieves an input 1dB compress point of +10.8 dBm, an IIP3 of +19.4 dBm, a DSB noise figure of 8 dB and a conversion gain of 1.5 dB.

articleTitle: Cascaded fourth-order mixed-coupled bandpass filter with good frequency selectivity
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A compact fourth-order bandpass filter with good frequency selectivity is presented. The proposed BPF consists of four cascaded stepped impedance resonators (SIRs). Mixed electric/magnetic (E/M) coupling are introduced in the proposed filter to generate transmission zeros (TZs) near the passband for sharp frequency selectivity. The method on the generation of transmission zeros caused by mixed coupling introduced in the filter is analyzed. A new filter with 15.4% fractional bandwidth (FBW) has been designed and fabricated to verify the validity of the proposed method. Three TZs are introduced near the passband, which is at 1.21GHz, 1.72GHz, 3.03GHz. Measured results are in good agreement with the electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: Design of ultrawideband planar monopole antenna of C shape
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel planar monopole with enhanced impedance performance across an ultrawideband operation bandwidth of 3.1–10.6GHz is proposed. With trimmed ground, this gradient CPW fed antenna is characterized by the rotated notch on the traditional ring monopole. By simply embedding this notch, the bandwidth of the ring monopole is widened remarkably from 2.3 to 16.8GHz. Notch related parameters analysis is carried out. Finally, experimental verification of the fabricated antenna for its impedance bandwidth is carried out, showing agreement with the simulated date.

articleTitle: Micro-Motions signatures analysis and extraction
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Micro-Doppler features can be regarded as a unique signature of an object with movements which provide additional information for classification, recognition and identification of the object. The common analysis method of Micro-Motion is time-frequency transform. However, the three-dimensional signatures of time-frequency distribution are not convenient to store and distinguish targets. The paper puts forward a general formula to match the signatures of time-frequency which will make the signatures reduce from three-dimensional to two-dimensional. Simulation study show the method is efficient for typical Micro-Motions such as vibration, wobbling, rotation, coning.

articleTitle: Design of a Ka-band GaN HEMT power amplifier based on simulation
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Based on the working mechanism of GaN components and monolithic microwave integrated power amplifiers, a four-stage and four-channel power amplifier design scheme has been realized by simulation in the paper. The physical structure of the GaN HEMT is proposed. Then DC and RF characteristics of the device are simulated in Silvaco. The S-parameters are extracted to design a power amplifier circuit in ADS according to the structure and electric performance of the HEMT. The results show that the output power of the amplifier circuit can reach 5.6W and the power gain is 21dB at 35GHz under CW condition. The PAE of the whole circuit is about 20%. Therefore, this power amplifier can be applied to Ka-band.

articleTitle: A design of ultra-low-voltage quadrature VCO
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A new quadrature voltage-controlled oscillator (QVCO) topology is proposed which consists of two same traditional low voltage-controlled oscillator and it is achieved by using back-gates coupling. The use of back-gates makes quadrature output clocks of voltage-controlled oscillator, reduces power dissipation and phase noise. That connecting the output terminal to the body terminal through resistor decreases the threshold voltage to low supply voltage. QVCO of the design use a standard 0.13 um 1P8M CMOS technology. At a supply voltage of 0.35 V, the total power dissipation is 2.60 mW. The frequency of output clock is 6.72 GHz.The phase noise at 1 MHz offset is -109.6 dBc/Hz, and the FOM(Figure-Of-Merit) is -182.0 dBc/Hz. The tuning range is from 6.21 GHz to 6.72 GHz. It is comparable or better than that of other state-of-the-art QVCO designs operating at much higher supply voltage.

articleTitle: Compact bandpass filter with improved stopband characteristics using S-L coupling
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A compact bandpass filter (BPF) with improved stopband performance using mixed electric/magnetic (E/M) coupling and Source-Load (S-L) coupling is presented. Due to the cancelling effect of the mixed coupling, a transmission zero (TZs) is employed near the passband. The design is implemented to a circular structure to achieve compact size. For realizing wide stopband characteristic, an extra transmission zero is achieved in the upper stopband owing to the S-L coupling introduced between the input and output port. A new filter centered at 1.08 GHz has been analyzed, simulated and fabricated to verify the validity of the proposed method. The measured results show that there are three finite transmission zeros near the passband, which are located at 0.78 GHz with 53.8 dB rejection, 1.86 GHz with 67.6 dB rejection, 3.01 GHz with 53.6 dB rejection, respectively. The out-of-band rejection better than 30 dB is up to 6 GHz. And the circuit only occupies 13.5×11.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of circularly polarized patch antenna array with H-shaped apertures
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A novel circularly polarization microstrip antenna array operated in S band is presented. The antenna array consists of four subarrays. The dual feeds are placed in orthogonal directions, and are connected to the Wilkinson power divider with the microstrip 90 degree phase shift between its two output feedlines. The patch is coupled by two orthogonal H-shaped apertures, which can enhance the isolation of the two ports and improve the circularly polarized performance. The antenna array gain is 14 dBic, the axial-ratio value within 3 dB is 45 degree and the cross-polarization levels in zenith direction are less than -23 dB at 1900 MHz. This results indicate that the proposed antenna realizes a good circularly polarization performance.

articleTitle: Antenna pattern arithmetic of unknown monopulse radar test
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Antenna pattern is an important performance index of radar, and the computation and drawing of antenna pattern occupies an important position in the test of radar. This paper introduces the antenna pattern drawing arithmetic of a portable radar test system, which using pulse width and repetition period to extract effectively pulses for the received unknown monopulse and then draw the antenna pattern. On this basis, using MATLAB software to simulate the radar test, program the code of calculation and draw, and give the antenna pattern and its parameters in the final.

articleTitle: Chebyshev transfer functions for the synthesis of an ultra-wideband(UWB) filter using short-circuit stub resonator
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, the Chebyshev transfer functions is proposed to synthesis and design a UWB filter using short-circuited stub resonator. A half wavelength transmission line with an embedded quarter wavelength short-circuited stub can be seen as a multi-modes resonator (MMR) to achieve a wide bandwidth, moreover, the embedded short-circuited stub can produce a pair of transmission zero to achieve a sharper rejection skirt. A UWB filter using short-circuited stub resonator is synthesized and simulated, the electromagnetic (EM) simulation results and the circuit simulation through the synthesis theory are almost the same.

articleTitle: Study and design of a 170GHz coaxial gyrotron cavity
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Based on mode coupling theory and numerical simulation, a comprehensive systematical study of high-frequency characteristics in a 170GHz smooth walled coaxial gyrotron cavity operating with mode is presented. In particular, the change of eigenvalues of operating mode, the coupling coefficients between different modes, the influence of mode coupling on diffraction quality factor and resonant frequency, the influence of single-mode and multi-mode coupling on high frequency field distribution as well as the phase of operating mode are investigated. The results show that the influence of the TM-type parasitic modes is extremely small, and can be ignored, but TE-type parasitic modes have some influences on diffraction quality factor of operating mode, that on resonant frequency of operating mode can be neglected.

articleTitle: A broadband circuit analog absorber based on printed dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Based on the equivalent transmission line theory, a composite absorber with broadband planar array antenna and AFSS is designed. The first layer is an array antenna, which uses printed dipole with balun feed as basic unit. The second layer is a AFSS, in which the traditional resistive layer is replaced with a PIN diode array, which corresponded with antenna feeding units. The impedance match characteristic of the absorber can be adjusted by adjusting the bias current of the PIN diode array. And the reflection characteristic of the composite absorber can be improved by printed dipole antenna array. Simulated by electromagnetic simulation software HFSS and CST, the results show that the composite absorber reflection coefficient is below -10dB at 3.5-15GHz. The experimental result is in good agreement with simulation data.

articleTitle: A compact wide stop band bandpass filter with loaded feeding structure
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: This paper presents a compact wide stop band bandpass filter using loaded feeding structure to enhance the out-of-band performance. The filter is constructed by three shorted parallel coupled stepped impendence resonators(SIRs), and is fed by tapping microstrip lines with open stubs loaded. The three order bandpass filter effectively suppresses the spurious pass band so that it has a so wide stop band. Measured results accord well with the simulated results, showing good performance of the filter.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of high temperature superconductor filters with 2nd harmonic suppression by using quasi-fractal resonators
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: This paper presents two filters based on quasi-fractal resonators. The first one is composed with resonators changed from Hilbert fractal resonators, the results show that this filter is smaller than the Hilbert fractal filter at a lower frequency and even more powerful in suppressing the 2nd harmonic. The other one with a cascaded quadruplet(CQ) structure is an 8-pole band pass elliptic filter based on L-shaped quasi-fractal resonators. The final structure of the second filter is only in half size of the usual meandered line filter and the 2nd harmonic suppression is much better than the meandered line filter. Results show that the proposed two filters are both possess good quality in transmission response and capable of size reduction and 2nd harmonic suppression.

articleTitle: Research on W-band Up-conversion module
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Up-conversion module is the core of transmitter, which plays a critical role in millimeter wave communication, radar, guidance and electronic warfare. This paper introduces the design and measurement of a W-band up-conversion module. W-band LO signal is obtained by frequency multiplying, then through up-conversion method, an X-band signal is converted to W-band. By fabricating, assembling and measuring, the experimental results indicate that the module's output RF power is more than 5 dBm at the RF frequency of 91∼95 GHz, power flatness is less than 3 dB and output linear dynamic range is more than 50 dB.

articleTitle: Multi-hop flocking algorithm for multi-agent system
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: With the time-delay of multi-hop communication taken into consideration, this paper proposes a multi-hop flocking algorithm for multi-agent system. Driven by the algorithm, agents broadcast both their own and neighbors' information in their communication ranging. The stability of algorithm and velocity matching property are analyzed theoretically. Comparing to the traditional ones, algorithm in this paper takes advantages of the multi-hop information and improves the velocity matching speed. A two-hop flocking algorithm is adopted in the numerical simulation and results give supports to the theoretical deduction.

articleTitle: Improved allocation algorithm schedules radar tasks parallel
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: Traditional single-computing is inefficient to meet the instantaneity requirement with the increasing of radar tasks' complexity; cluster computing is widely envisioned as a powerful paradigm for scheduling radar tasks parallel. An improved allocation algorithm is proposed for radar task allocation in distributed heterogeneous system. The continuous detection of task information of processors is put forward. Furthermore, task accumulation threshold is defined to estimate the processor is overloaded or not. In particular, the task will be allocated to the processors idle or light loading with the workload according to threshold. Simulation results show that executed time is reduced greatly and load balancing is improved immensely.

articleTitle: Single-layer frequency selective surface embedded with H-shape slots for stable performances
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, a single-layer bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) is proposed for L-band applications. The FSS unit cell consists of an improved hexagonal aperture unit embedded with H-shape slots. Simulated results show that the FSS obtains good frequency selective performance. Its relative bandwidth is about 55.7% using -3 dB as the criteria for the transmission coefficient. Moreover, the center frequency of the FSS structure remains stable at different incident angles for both TE and TM polarizations. The FSS retains excellent transmission characteristics even if the incident angle is up to 70 degree.

articleTitle: Existence of at least two positive periodic solutions of a modified Leslie-Gower predator-prey model with harvesting terms
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: In this paper, we study a modified Leslie-Gower predator-prey model with Holling II type functional response and harvesting terms. By means of the generalized continuation theorem, sufficient conditions for the existence of at least two positive periodic solutions of the model are established.

articleTitle: Compact dual-band CPW-fed antenna forWLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: A dual-band antenna forWLAN applications is proposed. The antenna consists of a CPW-fed and a mender line with a branch. The 2.4GHz resonant mode is generated by the long branch, while the 5.6GHz is generated by the short one. The proposed antenna has compact size of 30mm ×35 mm. The simulated return losses of the antenna are 510MHz (2.28GHz–2.77GHz) and 1300MHz (5GHz–6.3GHz), which is suitable for WLAN applications. A dual-band antenna for WLAN applications is proposed. The antenna consists of a CPW-fed and a mender line with a branch. The 2.4GHz resonant mode is generated by the long branch, while the 5.6GHz is generated by the short one. The proposed antenna has compact size of 30mm ×35 mm. The simulated return losses of the antenna are 510MHz (2.28GHz–2.77GHz) and 1300MHz (5GHz–6.3GHz), which is suitable for WLAN applications.

articleTitle: A new method of tracking group space object
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: It is imperative to efficiently track and catalogue the extensive dense group of space objects for space surveillance. As the main instrument for Low Earth Orbit space surveillance, ground-based radar systems are usually limited by their resolving power while tracking small, but very dense clusters of space debris. Thus, the information obtained regarding target detection and observation will be seriously compromised and overlapping, making the traditional multi-target tracking method inefficient. The traditional central group tracking can't get the information inside. Therefore, we conceived a new way to calculate the group center based on traditional group tracking model. By clustering the measurement in the echo gate of the group, the group center can be synthesized by the centers of clustering. The overall motion tendency is used to update the clustering within the group to obtain the distribution of the objects, and keep the tracking stable. Finally, the simulation of the tracking of group space objects is carried out to validate the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An accuracy test method for non-coaxial DUT
publicationTitle: 2013 International Workshop on Microwave and Millimeter Wave Circuits and System Technology
abstract: For non-coaxial DUT, accurate test depends on sophisticated and expensive test fixture. In addition, real-time of measurement results is not good. In this paper, we made a simple and practical, excellent performance of the PCB test fixture and the corresponding calibration standards for a LNA operating from 2000MHz to 2800MHz. According to TRL direct measurement method, de-embedding computing go directly on the VNA, and real-time de-embed measured results rendered. Experimental results show that a real-time and accurate measurement can be made for Non-coaxial DUT according to this method.
